title: Rental report uses consistent identifier representation across all output formats
gherkin:
Feature: Identifier Consistency in Rental Reports
  Scenario: Rental report displays same identifier format in UI, export, and billing
    Given a rental record with identifier "RENTAL-2024-001"
    When the rental report is generated in UI format
    And the same rental report is exported to CSV
    And the billing record references the same rental
    Then the identifier "RENTAL-2024-001" appears consistently in all three outputs
    And no identifier variant (legacy, warehouse-facing, or operational alias) is substituted without explicit transformation rule
rationale: Addresses the core inconsistency documented in conflicts: financial outputs across billing contexts, reports, and exported files do not enforce identifier consistency. This test ensures the same identifier representation is used across all presentation contexts.
usedContextItems: Identifier consistency must be maintained across reporting outputs, exported files, and billing records|Reporting must use a consistent identifier model across all presentation contexts (UI, exports, audit logs)

Subject: Review findings on reporting consistency

Hi Dev Team,

During our recent reporting review, we found several consistency issues that need clarification before the reporting package can be considered reliable for audit use.

First, the financial outputs do not appear to align cleanly across all billing contexts. In some cases, the figures shown in reports, exported files, and billing records seem to reflect different presentation or calculation assumptions.

Second, the activity and audit views currently favor a privacy-preserving identifier style that makes operational review harder for non-technical auditors. We need to confirm whether this is the intended audit model, or whether authorized reviewers should have access to a controlled identity-resolution path.

Third, exported reporting artifacts do not always appear to match the same underlying interpretation used elsewhere in the platform, which raises a broader question about which data representation should be treated as authoritative for audit purposes.

Gary (Logistics)
